summary: Both round-1 findings are fixed and independently verified with fresh repros against an isolated `git worktree --detach 0becb36` checkout (the shared tree had again been edited concurrently during this round, same as round 1 — redirected all test execution to the clean worktree). SEC-CG-1 (HIGH): the idempotent-ALTER loop is now `_ensure_column()` — check via `pragma_table_info(?)` (table-valued function, parameterised) -> ALTER only if genuinely missing -> re-read and confirm -- applied uniformly to all five migrated columns via a `_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` tuple. Only `duplicate column name` is tolerated as benign; anything else (including `database is locked`) is logged at ERROR and raised as `SchemaMigrationError`. Reproduced the exact real prod-upgrade scenario end to end: a DB with the four pre-existing columns (telegraph_url/telegraph_path/model_fingerprint x2, i.e. what live prod actually has today) but WITHOUT `hold_reason`, racing a writer holding a real IMMEDIATE lock past the 5s busy_timeout -- the migration now fails LOUDLY (`SchemaMigrationError: could not add column pending_articles.hold_reason: database is locked`), with a clean `pending_articles_repo ERROR schema migration failed: ...` log line emitted first, and the column confirmed still absent afterward (no silent corruption). Also verified: (a) happy path -- a fresh DB migrates cleanly, all 5 columns present; (b) idempotent re-run -- traced actual SQL via `set_trace_callback` and confirmed a second `init_schema()` call on an already-migrated DB issues exactly 5 `pragma_table_info` existence checks and ZERO ALTER statements; (c) the realistic prod-upgrade shape specifically -- exactly ONE ALTER runs (for hold_reason only) and is verified present afterward, no interference with the other four already-migrated columns. The project's own new `TestColumnMigrationHardening` suite (pending_articles_repo tests) independently covers the same ground with a REAL lock (not a mocked exception, matching the commit's claim) plus `test_a_swallowed_lock_would_break_the_publish_path`, which pins the exact consequence (count_pending/list_pending/list_held all raise `no such column: hold_reason` when the guard is bypassed) -- this is the right regression anchor for the severity argument. SEC-CG-2 (MEDIUM): tokens now carry a kind (`<kind>|<link>` value, migration-free -- legacy bare-link values with no separator/unknown prefix correctly fall back to `dedup`, verified including the adversarial case of a legacy link whose value happens to start with a non-kind prefix containing `|`, e.g. `'ftp|http://x/c'`, which correctly reads as a dedup link rather than being misparsed). Both resolvers (`resolve_dedup_callback`, `resolve_hold_callback`) now check `get_review_token(token)[0]` against their own expected kind FIRST and answer the existing safe `⚠️ Кнопка устарела` on a mismatch. Reproduced both original directions again end-to-end against a real SQLite DB: (1) a dedup-minted token redeemed via `resolve_hold_callback('reject'/'approve', ...)` -- now correctly refused, the ordinary article is NOT deleted, and the token is NOT consumed; (2) a hold-minted token redeemed via `resolve_dedup_callback('keep'/'cancel', ...)` -- now correctly refused, `hold_reason` stays unchanged, and the token is NOT consumed. In both directions, immediately replaying the SAME token through its CORRECT resolver afterward still works normally and consumes the token as expected -- proving the mismatch path is a true no-op, not a soft-lock. A URL containing `|` in the query string (`http://x/a?q=1|2|3`) round-trips intact through `put_review_token`/`get_review_token`/`resolve_hold_callback('approve', ...)`, confirming the first-separator-only split does not mangle it. The project's own new tests (`TestReviewTokenKinds`, and `test_dedup_token_redeemed_by_the_hold_resolver_is_refused` / `test_hold_token_redeemed_by_the_dedup_resolver_is_refused` / `test_cross_grammar_refusal_runs_after_the_admin_gate` in test_integration.py) match this coverage almost exactly, plus an extra check I hadn't separately verified in round 1 -- that the admin gate still runs BEFORE the kind check, so a non-admin press against a mismatched-kind token still returns bare `(None, "")` rather than confirming the token's existence via a kind-mismatch answer. Full suite: 1553 passed, 354 subtests passed, deterministic across 3 consecutive full runs in the isolated worktree (matching the commit message's own claim of determinism after fixing an unrelated tearDown-ordering test flake). Also spot-checked the F1/F2 video-subject-rule rewrite (not part of my original findings, but new code in this same commit): the two new regexes are anchored, alternation-only (no nested quantifiers), timed clean against adversarial padding/repetition (sub-millisecond), and only ever run on text already bounded to 2000 chars by the pre-existing `_promo_scan_input`/`_content_gate_subject` pipeline; re-ran ~25 non-str/malformed-input repros against the updated `_is_rejected_genre` and the new `_genre_video_subject_marker` helper -- zero exceptions, same fail-open coercion behaviour as before. No new security-relevant regression found there.

findings_disposition.verification: Reproduced the exact realistic prod-upgrade scenario (4 pre-existing columns, hold_reason missing, real IMMEDIATE-lock contention past the 5s busy_timeout) end-to-end: migration now raises `pending_articles_repo.SchemaMigrationError: could not add column pending_articles.hold_reason: database is locked`, preceded by a `pending_articles_repo ERROR schema migration failed: could not add pending_articles.hold_reason (OperationalError: database is locked)` log line -- diagnosable and attributable, not silent. Column confirmed still absent afterward (correctly not mistaken for success). Separately verified the happy path (concurrent writer held <5s -> waits it out, no error, migration lands) and idempotency (traced actual SQL via sqlite3's `set_trace_callback`: a second `init_schema()` call on an already-migrated DB issues 5 `pragma_table_info` reads and 0 ALTER statements; repeated 3x with no drift). Verified the specific 'prod scenario' request literally: staged a DB with exactly the 4 pre-existing columns and confirmed exactly 1 ALTER statement runs (for hold_reason) and is verified present afterward, with the other 4 untouched.
findings_disposition.residual_risk: None in the reviewed migration path itself. One clarifying, non-blocking observation recorded as a new checks_performed note (not a new finding): init_db()'s OTHER schema-creation statements -- the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS processed_news` in news_bot.init_db() and the four `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` calls inside init_schema() for pending/published/failed/bot_state -- are outside `_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` and were never wrapped in the old silent-swallow pattern to begin with, so this is not a regression and not in scope for SEC-CG-1 (which targeted the ADD COLUMN idempotency bug specifically). Under sufficiently severe lock contention they can still raise a raw, un-namespaced `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` before `_ensure_column` is ever reached (reproduced this by racing a lock against a truly-fresh, zero-tables DB) -- worth the operator knowing that a startup crash may show a bare OperationalError rather than the nicer SchemaMigrationError message, but the safety property that matters (fails loudly, never silently corrupts) holds either way.

findings_disposition.verification: Re-ran both original repro directions against the fixed code with a real SQLite DB: (1) `put_review_token(tok, ordinary_link, kind=DEDUP)` then `resolve_hold_callback('reject', tok, admin)` -> now `('⚠️ Кнопка устарела', ...)`, article confirmed NOT deleted, token confirmed NOT consumed (get_review_token_link still resolves); the SAME token then correctly resolves via `resolve_dedup_callback('keep', ...)` afterward, proving the correct button still works. (2) `put_review_token(tok, held_link, kind=HOLD)` then `resolve_dedup_callback('keep', tok, admin)` -> refused the same way, hold_reason confirmed unchanged ('poster', still held), token confirmed NOT consumed; the SAME token then correctly resolves via `resolve_hold_callback('approve', ...)` afterward, clearing hold_reason and publishing it into the queue -- proving the held article is not orphaned. Additionally tested a URL containing '|' end-to-end (mint via HOLD kind, read back, approve) -- link preserved byte-for-byte, hold_reason correctly cleared. Confirmed legacy bare-link bot_state values (no kind prefix, written before this change) still read back as ('dedup', link).
findings_disposition.residual_risk: None found. The one theoretical edge case I considered -- a legacy bare-link value that coincidentally starts with the literal string 'dedup|' or 'hold|' followed by more text, which would be misread as kind-prefixed -- requires a URL to literally begin with one of those two exact strings rather than a scheme (`http://`, etc.), which is not a realistic URL shape; the project's own new test `test_unknown_prefix_is_treated_as_a_legacy_link` additionally confirms any OTHER pipe-containing legacy value (e.g. 'ftp|http://x/c') correctly falls through to the dedup/legacy branch rather than being misparsed, which is the actually-reachable version of this edge case and it behaves correctly.

additional_checks_performed: Ran the full suite 3x in an isolated `git worktree --detach 0becb36` (the shared working tree was again being edited by a concurrent process during this round, same contamination pattern as round 1) -- 1553 passed, 354 subtests passed, deterministic all 3 runs, ~20-24s each -- matches the commit message's claim of 'deterministic across 6 consecutive full runs' and its claim of fixing an unrelated addCleanup/tearDown-ordering test flake.

Ran the project's own new regression suites directly: `pytest tests/test_pending_articles_repo.py::TestColumnMigrationHardening tests/test_database.py` -> 24 passed, 13 subtests; `pytest tests/test_pending_articles_repo.py::TestReviewTokenKinds` -> 9 passed; `pytest tests/test_integration.py -k "Grammars or Kind or kind"` -> 8 passed, 19 subtests -- all green, and read each test body to confirm they exercise the same failure modes as my own repros (a real IMMEDIATE lock for SEC-CG-1's `test_locked_db_during_alter_raises_instead_of_silently_passing`, and the exact two cross-grammar directions for SEC-CG-2) rather than being weaker mocked stand-ins.

Read `test_a_swallowed_lock_would_break_the_publish_path` -- confirms the project itself pins the severity argument by asserting count_pending/list_pending/list_held all raise `sqlite3.OperationalError` naming 'hold_reason' if the guard were ever bypassed, which is exactly the blast-radius reasoning SEC-CG-1 was rated HIGH on.

Traced exactly which code path fails first under lock contention at container-startup scale (a truly fresh, zero-migrated-column DB): it is `news_bot.init_db()`'s pre-existing, unmodified `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS processed_news` statement, not `_ensure_column` -- confirms this is out of scope for SEC-CG-1 (never had the silent-swallow bug) and is not a regression; re-ran the SAME probe against the realistic single-missing-column prod scenario and confirmed the failure correctly surfaces through `_ensure_column`/`SchemaMigrationError` with full logging in that case, as designed.

Answered the coordinator's specific 'does it crash cleanly or crash-loop silently' question by tracing both `init_db()` call sites (`main()` at startup, `job()` every tick) and confirmed neither is wrapped in try/except; a `SchemaMigrationError` propagates to the top-level `if __name__ == "__main__": main()` uncaught, printing a full traceback (captured by Docker's json-file logging driver) and exiting the process; docker-compose.yml's `restart: unless-stopped` then restarts the container. For the realistic trigger (a transient lock that has almost certainly cleared by restart time) this is very likely self-healing after one restart cycle. For a persistent condition (disk full, readonly volume) it becomes a genuine crash-loop, but a DIAGNOSABLE one -- every cycle logs the specific table/column/error -- versus the old behaviour's crash-loop on an unrelated-looking 'no such column' error with zero attribution. No Telegram alert fires for this specific failure (it happens before any of main()'s own best-effort notification code runs); the pre-existing, unmodified heartbeat-file/watchdog.sh mechanism (external host cron, mentioned in the Dockerfile) is the existing fallback detection path for any total-crash scenario, not something unique to this diff.

Spot-checked the F1/F2 video-subject-rule rewrite (new code in this commit, not part of my original findings) for security regressions: timed the two new anchored alternation regexes (`_GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_SEP_RE`, `_GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_NP_RE`) against adversarial padding/repetition inputs -- sub-millisecond, no backtracking blowup; confirmed both only ever run on `raw_title` already bounded to 2000 chars by the existing `_promo_scan_input` pipeline (a marker placed past the cap is still not detected); re-ran ~25 non-str/malformed-input repros (non-str link as list/dict/int/float/bool/bytes/None, non-str title, entry/article as None/str/list) against the updated `_is_rejected_genre` and the new `_genre_video_subject_marker` -- zero exceptions in all cases.

Confirmed the admin_alerts.py refactor unifying E035/E036/E037 title/marker rendering into shared `_intake_alert_title`/`_intake_alert_markers` preserves the exact same truncation (200 chars + ellipsis) and constants-only-marker-rendering safety properties verified in round 1 -- pure de-duplication, no behavioural change to the audited alert-content protections.

prod_migration_go_no_go: GO, no residual blockers. Both round-1 findings are fixed and independently reproduced-and-verified-fixed against the exact realistic prod-upgrade scenario (4 pre-existing columns + missing hold_reason, real lock contention). The migration now fails loudly and diagnosably instead of silently corrupting the schema, and the cross-grammar token confusion now refuses cleanly without mutating state or burning tokens in either direction. The only remaining note is informational: a `SchemaMigrationError` (or, in the rare all-fresh-DB case, a raw `sqlite3.OperationalError` from an unrelated pre-existing CREATE TABLE statement) at startup will crash the container and rely on Docker's `restart: unless-stopped` to recover, with no immediate Telegram ping specific to this failure -- an acceptable, pre-existing operational pattern for this app (consistent with how every other unhandled-exception crash already behaves, and backed by the existing external heartbeat/watchdog mechanism), not something this migration needs to solve on its own. Optional, non-blocking polish for a future pass: a best-effort admin-notification attempt wrapped specifically around the two `init_db()` call sites would shave the detection latency for this one failure mode, but is not required to ship.
